steps.user_message: I have a legal situation I need help thinking through. It's related to contract dispute with a former employer. I'm working with Maria Santos from Santos Law Office; our next step is family court in Denver. Timeline: The judge set a status conference in two months.. The other party is the respondent in the case. We're in San Diego County, California. I have documentation but I'm not sure what else the court will want. I'd like to know what I should ask my lawyer regarding whether I need to get more evidence before the next date. This is private legal business.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with legal-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can help you prepare. A couple quick clarifying points before detailed suggestions:
- You said “family court in Denver” but also “San Diego County, California.” Which court will actually hear the status conference? (Jurisdiction and local rules affect what the court will ask for.)
- Do you want me to draft an email to Maria Santos listing these questions and asking whether you should gather more evidence? I won’t send anything without your permission.

Below are focused questions you can ask Maria Santos (grouped and prioritized) to determine whether you need more evidence before the status conference, plus immediate steps you can take now.

Questions to ask your lawyer (priorities first)
- Case scope & next hearing
  - Which court and judge will handle the status conference, and what local rules/forms should we follow for that date?
  - What is the goal of the status conference (scheduling only, settlement discussion, dispute over evidence, temporary relief)?
- Evidence sufficiency & gaps
  - Based on what we currently have, do we have the evidence needed to establish each essential element of our claims/defenses? If not, what’s missing?
  - Which specific document types will be most persuasive (contracts, pay records, performance reviews, emails, text messages, payroll records, termination letters, payment history)?
- Admissibility & authentication
  - Are our existing documents likely to be admissible? Do any need witness authentication, business-records certification, or a custodian declaration?
  - Do any digital items require forensic preservation or metadata to prove authenticity (email headers, file timestamps)?
- Preservation & spoliation
  - Should we send a preservation/preservation-letter to the respondent or third parties now?
  - Do we need to immediately preserve original documents, devices, or accounts? Any risk of spoliation?
- Discovery & timing
  - What discovery should we open now (document requests, interrogatories, admissions, subpoenas)? What are the relevant deadlines?
  - Are depositions or expert reports likely to be needed before the next status conference?
- Witnesses & testimony
  - Whose testimony would help (co-workers, HR, third-party vendors)? Should we obtain sworn statements or declarations now?
  - Should we identify and contact witnesses now to preserve their recollection?
- Experts & valuation
  - Do we need an expert (accountant, employment expert, forensic IT) and how long to retain/prep one?
- Court filings & exhibits
  - Will the court ask for an exhibit list or pre-conference filings? If so, what format is required?
  - Do we need proposed orders or a proposed schedule ready for the status conference?
- Strategy & cost-benefit
  - Given the facts, what evidence is high-value vs low-value (and what is worth the time/cost to obtain)?
  - Are settlement or ADR steps recommended before the conference?
- Tactical / emergency moves
  - Should we seek a protective order, temporary relief, or an interim hearing before the status conference?

Concrete actions you can take now (before you confirm with counsel)
- Preserve originals and make backups: secure original documents and take high-quality scans; create redundant encrypted backups.
- Create a clear chronology/timeline: one page with dates, actions, who did what — this helps your lawyer spot holes quickly.
- Consolidate communications: gather emails, texts, Slack messages, voicemail records; export full headers for important emails.
- Capture witness recollections: short written statements of what each witness saw (date, signature, ideally notarized or at least dated).
- Document business records: ask custodians (HR, payroll) for certified copies, or note how to subpoena if needed.
- Label and paginate exhibits: number pages, create an exhibit list with short descriptions and Bates numbers so counsel can assess gaps.
- Preserve devices/accounts: do not delete anything from relevant phones/computers; take screenshots and note account details.
- Consider quick expert screening: if numbers/economic harm matter, ask counsel whether a preliminary accountant review would be helpful.
- Ask counsel about a preservation letter: if counsel recommends, have them send a preservation letter to avoid spoliation.

A short checklist you can hand your lawyer
- Contract(s) and amendments (originals and signed copies)
- All communications (email, text, messaging apps) with dates and headers
- Payment & payroll records, invoices, bank transfers
- Termination/disciplinary notices, performance reviews
- Witness names, contact info, short statements
- Any third-party records you may need to subpoena (HR files, server logs)
- Digital evidence: exports of email headers, metadata where relevant
- Timeline document and proposed exhibit list

Other practical reminders
- Confirm local court procedures (some courts require exhibit lists or exchange before status conferences).
- Ask Maria how she prefers to receive the materials (PDF with bookmarks, physical binder, shared folder).
- Ask whether counsel wants originals or certified copies — don’t send originals until instructed.

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a concise email to Maria Santos that lists these questions and your current documents (I’ll wait for your go-ahead and the exact email address to use).
- Create a one-page timeline template or exhibit list you can fill and share with counsel.
- Help organize the documents into a labeled PDF or prepare a witness statement template.

Which of the above would you like me to do next? And please confirm the correct court (Denver or San Diego) so I can tailor recommendations to local rules.
